acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust supplies page alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload copy and metadata. Profile/message text uses one transparent shared Metal underlay, native typography/color services, static AX/layout adapters and Rust body layout. Native dialog window/title/button painting, default-key/modal policy and all browser authority remain adapters.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Rust PageDialogCopy supplies display title/profile identity, bounded message UTF-16, accept/cancel captions, prompt/cancel presence and stored default-cancel metadata. It receives only display origin/profile strings, dialog kind/unload flags and message units. Native active-frame/window/visibility/profile validation, requesting frame/generation tracking, modal authorization and renderer callbacks remain unchanged. No returned display string is used for browser authority.

The message cap remains exactly 8192 UTF-16 units, preserving even a boundary-cut surrogate as the original substring did. Prompt initial/answer text continues to use the existing editor independently of the display-message cap. Native buttons/title frame remain native controls, with their labels and flags projected from Rust in the opt-in backend.

Profile and message copy reuse the preference/tools static-text adapter and one transparent underlay per dialog body. Native label typography/colors, centered profile identity, left multiline message, fixed SizeToFit(440) preferred-size semantics, 220px message scroll cap, 480px body width and 280px minimum preferred height remain. No native Label or hidden measuring Label is created for these two body text roles. Native buttons/title controls outside that body remain.

Single-line center alignment is an explicit flag in the existing static-text recipe; old callers retain left alignment. A native-typography option uses the current native label font/color service and updates on theme changes. Standalone RenderText still measures line boundaries. CPU recipe fallback remains when the shared Metal canvas is absent.

The message scroll retains native event/scroll/AX services with explicit scroll synchronization and a callback to refresh scene clips. The shared underlay stays below the prompt canvas and excludes its input rectangle. Native modal widget, native buttons, platform Return/Escape/default-cancel behavior, IME admission, stale-response/cancellation and synchronous-close callback rules remain.

The scene owner is destroyed before the widget. Weak scene callbacks and scroll subscriptions are invalidated before body text/scroll views disappear; the native manager still posts renderer callbacks off the button stack. Tests verify CloseNow destroys the prompt text client and scene, then a fresh dialog contains no old scene text.

Two Rust cases cover dialog metadata, Unicode/UTF-16 cap and explicit center/left primitives. A shared browser test covers alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload title/button/default/prompt roles, static AX copy, childlessness versus native Labels, native preferred-size/height oracles, and once-only callbacks. A dedicated Metal test checks actual scene text, layer order, prompt cutout, long-message start/end culling, real scrolling, native theme changes, CloseNow and reopening. Existing real Cocoa IME/default/override/stale-frame/navigation and beforeunload contracts remain in the critical gate.

No crate/library/dependency or browser-service operation changed. Native dialog title/buttons and container/window/event/focus/AX/scroll ownership remain to migrate; this does not complete page-dialog UI ownership.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
